title: The Letter to Philemon
lead: Paul's shortest letter, written from prison to Philemon, a believer whose house was a church's meeting place, about Onesimus, a slave of his household who had become a believer through Paul. Paul asks Philemon to receive him "no longer as a slave, but as more than a slave: a much-loved brother," and offers to pay his debts. Almost all scholars accept it as Paul's, and it has been at the center of the Christian argument over slavery.

sections.b: A greeting to Philemon, Apphia, Archippus and the church in the house (1:1-3); thanks for Philemon's love (1:4-7); the appeal for Onesimus, once useless and now useful, sent back to be had back forever as a brother (1:8-16); "Welcome him as if he were me," with Paul's signed promise to pay (1:17-22); greetings and blessing (1:23-25).

Colossians names the same people and sends Onesimus home with Tychicus, so the letter is usually placed at Colossae. Where Paul was held (Ephesus, Caesarea or Rome) and how Onesimus came to him (a runaway, a slave seeking his master's friend as mediator, a helper sent by the church, or, on one reading, not a slave at all) are debated. The book page and the chapter page set out each view.
